title: Flu vaccine
what: A vaccine injection in your upper arm. It helps your body get ready for the flu in advance. You cannot catch the flu from this vaccine.
why: Every year before flu season, usually in the fall. Especially important for children, older people, pregnant women, and people with long-term illnesses.
duration: the shot takes a few seconds, usually 15 to 40 minutes with the checkup
tell_doctor: If you are ill now or have a fever
Allergies, especially strong reactions to past vaccines
Immune system problems or treatment that weakens it

prepare.title: Health
prepare.text: The vaccine is given when you are well. You will have a quick check before the shot.

prepare.title: Timing
prepare.text: It is best to get vaccinated early, before the flu season starts. Protection builds up in about 2 weeks.

prepare.title: Clothes
prepare.text: Wear something comfortable so your upper arm is easy to uncover.

bring: Your vaccination record, if you have one
steps: The doctor or nurse asks how you feel and takes your temperature
The skin is wiped and the shot is given
The vaccine is written in your records
After the shot, you stay at the clinic for about 30 minutes
feel: Sometimes the spot is sore or red for 1 to 2 days
Sometimes tiredness or a mild fever. It goes away on its own
after: Stay near the room for 30 minutes
You can go back to your usual day
Do not rub the injection spot
Protection builds up in about 2 weeks and lasts about a year
red_flags: Trouble breathing, a swollen face or throat, or a rash all over the body: call emergency services
A high fever that lasts more than two days

faq.q: Can the flu shot give me the flu?
faq.a: No. The vaccine has no live virus that can cause the flu. Feeling a bit tired is your immune system responding.

faq.q: Why do I need a flu shot every year?
faq.a: The flu virus changes, and the vaccine is updated every season. Protection from last year's shot also fades.

faq.q: Can I get the flu shot while pregnant?
faq.a: Usually yes, it is recommended. Tell your doctor you are pregnant. They will choose the vaccine and timing.
